item.title: Vicksburg business owner offers $5,000 reward after zero-turn mowers stolen - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Therese Apel
item.description:
VICKSBURG — The owner of a Vicksburg powersports business is offering a $5,000 reward after thieves allegedly cut through a fence and stole three zero-turn mowers early Monday morning.

Allen Pugh, owner of Patriot Motorsports, said the burglary happened around 3:45 a.m. at the business in Vicksburg.

According to Pugh, surveillance footage showed suspects parking across the street near a co-op around 2:30 a.m. before allegedly cutting the business’s fence and stealing three Scag zero-turn mowers. The suspects reportedly left the area around 4:27 a.m.

Pugh said the suspects were driving what he described as a distinctive white Ram 3500 or 4500 one-ton flatbed truck equipped with cab lights and front fender flares. He said the truck did not display a license plate.

The business owner also said he believes the same truck was used in a burglary at a mower dealership in Collins last week and had previously been connected to another break-in at Patriot Motorsports. Pugh said equipment stolen during the earlier incident was later recovered in Memphis, though no arrests were made.

Pugh initially believed the suspects may have crossed the Mississippi River bridge but later posted that the truck most likely traveled into Hinds County after leaving the area southbound on U.S. 61. He said it remains unclear whether the suspects traveled toward Highway 27, Highway 80 or Interstate 20.

The owner is asking anyone with surveillance cameras between Vicksburg and the Beechwood intersection to review footage for possible sightings of the truck.

In a later social media post, Pugh shared a photo of cash and reiterated his offer of a $5,000 reward for information leading to the recovery of the equipment or identification of the suspects.

Darkhorse Press has reached out to the Vicksburg Police Department for additional information and will update this story when more details become available.

item.title: UPDATE: 26 injuries reported after tornadoes impact Mississippi - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
JACKSON – Twenty-six injuries have been reported after tornadoes moved through Mississippi, Gov. Tate Reeves said in an update on storm recovery efforts.

Reeves said 22 injuries were reported in Lincoln County, three in Lamar County and one in Franklin County. The Mississippi State Department of Health is expected to meet with hospitals to help assess the status of those injured.

Power outages statewide have dropped to about 1,460, down from a peak of about 20,100, Reeves said. Utility crews continue working to restore power.

In Lincoln County, eight roads remain impassable because of debris. Damage assessments are expected to take place, with support from Hinds, Covington, Jones and Forrest counties, as well as the Mississippi Emergency Management Agency.

The American Red Cross shelter in Brookhaven had no occupants overnight, according to Reeves. Two points of distribution remain open at the Bogue Chitto Fire Department and East Lincoln Fire Department.

Feeding operations also continue at the Bogue Chitto Fire Department, East Lincoln Fire Department, Auburn Road near Calvary Road and Bogue Chitto Baptist Church.

Samaritan’s Purse has opened a volunteer intake site at Pleasant Hill Baptist Church. Volunteer orientations are being held at 7:30 a.m. and 12:30 p.m. daily, as needed.

A donation intake center is located at the Lincoln County School District building at 702 Saints Trail NW in Brookhaven.

In Lamar County, damage assessments are complete, and electric power associations continue working to restore power. Debris removal continues on roadways. A safe room has been moved to standby status and can reopen if needed.

The American Red Cross, The Salvation Army, Samaritan’s Purse, Mississippi Baptist Relief, Temple Baptist and others are assisting with recovery efforts.

In Franklin County, damage assessments are complete, roadways remain passable and the emergency operations center has returned to normal operations, Reeves said.

Reeves thanked volunteers, first responders, utility crews and emergency managers assisting with recovery efforts across the state.

item.title: Two Texas men arrested after Pearl River County checkpoint - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
PEARL RIVER COUNTY – Two Texas men were arrested after Pearl River County deputies found suspected drugs and a firearm during a safety checkpoint, authorities said.

The Pearl River County Sheriff’s Department said deputies conducted a safety checkpoint April 30 on Highway 43 near Sycamore Road in Picayune.

At about 11:51 p.m., deputies stopped a vehicle traveling through the checkpoint after detecting the odor of marijuana, according to the sheriff’s department. Investigators said deputies later found suspected controlled substances and a firearm inside the vehicle.

The driver was identified as Charlie Randall, 66, of Cedar Hill, Texas. The passenger was identified as Joseph Brooks, 65, of Dallas.

Deputies said they recovered suspected marijuana, cocaine and oxycodone, along with a .25-caliber handgun. Authorities said criminal history checks showed both men are convicted felons.

Randall and Brooks were taken to the Lenoir Rowell Criminal Justice Center. Both were charged with two felony counts of possession of a controlled substance while in possession of a firearm and possession of a weapon by a convicted felon.

Anyone with information about illegal activity is asked to contact the Pearl River County Sheriff’s Office at 601-403-2582.

item.title: Samaritan’s Purse offering tornado cleanup assistance in Lincoln County - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
BOGUE CHITTO – Samaritan’s Purse is offering free cleanup assistance to homeowners in Lincoln County affected by recent tornadoes.

The organization said volunteers may be able to help with chainsaw work, temporary roof tarping, personal property and furniture removal, debris cleanup, flood cleanup and sanitizing through Shockwave treatment.

Priority will be given to homeowners who are uninsured or underinsured. Requests will be handled based on need and volunteer availability.

Residents seeking assistance may call 833-747-1234 to speak with a Samaritan’s Purse representative.

The organization is operating locally out of Pleasant Hill Baptist Church, located at 2305 Pleasant Hill Drive SE in Bogue Chitto.

Volunteer opportunities also are available. Those interested in serving may call 601-967-5511 or visit spvolunteer.org.

item.title: Natchez teen among two killed in Louisiana crash; driver arrested - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
CONCORDIA PARISH – Louisiana State Police are investigating a single-vehicle crash in Concordia Parish that killed two people early Sunday, according to KNOE.

The crash happened shortly after 12:30 a.m. May 10 on Minorca Road.

State police said 18-year-old Gregory Steele was driving north on Minorca Road when he lost control of the vehicle, left the roadway and overturned.

Authorities said two passengers, 17-year-old Michelle Baity of Natchez, Mississippi, and 19-year-old Jacob Bonnette of Vidalia, died from injuries suffered in the crash.

According to state police, none of the people in the vehicle were wearing seat belts. Steele suffered minor injuries. Another passenger, who also was not wearing a seat belt, suffered moderate injuries and was taken to a local hospital.

Investigators said impairment is suspected to be a factor in the crash, and samples were submitted for testing.

Steele was arrested on two counts of vehicular homicide, underage driving while intoxicated, vehicular negligent injuring and careless operation, according to KNOE.

The crash remains under investigation.

item.title: MS Insurance Department: Homeowners should prepare now for wildfire risk, review coverage - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Therese Apel
item.description:
JACKSON — Mississippi may not be the first state that comes to mind for wildfires, but the Mississippi Insurance Department is warning homeowners the risk is real, and that preparing now could mean the difference between losing a home and saving one.

The department recommends homeowners create what’s known as a “defensible space”, which is a buffer between a home and surrounding vegetation, and review their insurance policies to ensure wildfire coverage is in place before disaster strikes.

The Insurance Institute for Business and Home Safety recommends the following steps to create defensible space:

On the insurance side, standard homeowners policies typically cover repair or replacement of a home’s structure and items damaged by flames, smoke, soot and ash, but Insurance Commissioner and State Fire Marshal Mike Chaney said policyholders should not assume they are fully covered.

“Most homeowners and renters policies help with recovery expenses through additional living expense coverage, known as ALE,” Chaney said. “While a homeowners policy may provide a benefit during a mandatory evacuation, some insurance companies impose conditions such as waiting periods or actual damage to your property.”

ALE coverage typically includes extra food and housing costs, furniture rental, relocation and storage, and transportation expenses. Chaney advised policyholders to keep all receipts for submission to their insurance company.

Homeowners should also document the contents of their home now, before any disaster occurs. The National Association of Insurance Commissioners offers a free Home Inventory App at content.naic.org/consumer/home-inventory .

item.title: Mizzou RB Ahmad Hardy shot at Mississippi concert, reported in stable condition - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Therese Apel
item.description:
MISSISSIPPI — University of Missouri running back Ahmad Hardy was shot at a concert somewhere in Mississippi in the early morning hours Sunday, the university announced Monday, and is listed in stable condition following surgery.

Mizzou Athletics confirmed Hardy sustained a gunshot wound but did not disclose the location of the concert or additional details surrounding the shooting. No law enforcement information has been made public.

“Ahmad is deeply loved by his teammates, coaches, friends, family and fans,” the university said in a statement. “We will continue to stand beside him and his family through this difficult time, offering our love, prayers, strength and support.”

The university said a timeline for Hardy’s return to football activities is unknown and that it will provide updates as information becomes available.

Hardy, a Lawrence County High School graduate, led the SEC with 1,649 rushing yards and 16 touchdowns in 2025, earning All-American, SEC Newcomer of the Year and All-SEC honors. He set a Missouri single-season rushing record and transferred to the Tigers after spending the 2024 season at Louisiana-Monroe. Hardy was ranked the No. 1 RB in the SEC ahead of the 2026 season by SEC Country.

ESPN is reporting that a source told them that Hardy was alert Monday and moving around, and there is optimism that he will play football again, though the extent of any impact on his football future has not been determined

The location of the concert has not been confirmed. This story will be updated as information becomes available.

item.title: Mississippi officials to host annual Fallen Officers Candlelight Vigil in Jackson - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Therese Apel
item.description:
JACKSON — Attorney General Lynn Fitch, the Mississippi Sheriffs’ Association and the Mississippi Association of Chiefs of Police will host the 16th annual Fallen Officers Candlelight Vigil on Tuesday in observance of National Police Week.

The ceremony is scheduled for 6 p.m. May 12 at the Mississippi Fallen Officers Memorial, located between the Mississippi Supreme Court and the Walter Sillers Building near High Street in Jackson.

Officials said the annual vigil honors Mississippi law enforcement officers who lost their lives in the line of duty.

Scheduled speakers include Fitch; Sean Tindell, commissioner of the Mississippi Department of Public Safety; William “Billy” Seal of the Long Beach Police Department; and Randy Tucker of the Madison County Sheriff’s Department.

item.title: Meridian Police investigate fatal shooting early Sunday morning - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Cash Matlock
item.description:
MERIDIAN — The Meridian Police Department is investigating a fatal shooting that occurred early Sunday morning in the 800 block of 45th Avenue.

Police said officers were already patrolling an event in the area at approximately 1:30 a.m. when an altercation reportedly occurred inside a local business.

According to investigators, security personnel removed an individual from the business following the disturbance.

Investigators said the altercation then escalated in the parking lot of the Council of Organizations building, where one person, identified as Zaqwavion Carlisle, was shot.

Carlisle was transported to a local hospital, where he later died.

The Meridian Police Department Criminal Investigations Division continues to investigate the incident. Additional information will be released as it becomes available.

Police are asking anyone who may have video recordings of the incident or information related to the case to contact investigators at 601-485-1893 or 769-298-5111. Individuals also may contact Crime Stoppers anonymously or email information and footage to [email protected]

item.title: Meridian Community College expands workforce training with automotive technology program - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Special to Darkhorse Press
item.description:
JACKSON – Responding to growing demand in Mississippi’s automotive sector, Meridian Community College is launching a new automotive technology program made possible through support from AccelerateMS.

Students will receive hands-on training in core automotive systems and emerging technologies. Instruction meets Automotive Service Excellence standards and emphasizes safety, employability skills, and work-based learning to prepare graduates for successful careers.

The investment supports a new two-year Associate of Applied Science degree in Automotive Technology developed in response to regional employer needs. The program offers flexible one-year and two-year exit points, allowing students to enter the workforce or continue toward advanced credentials. Once fully scaled, the program will add up to 15 new student seats per year, resulting in up to 30 additional seats.

With a combination of state and federal investments, the college is expanding training capacity and equipping students with the tools and technology needed for hands-on, high-quality instruction. MCC was awarded more than $300,000 from AccelerateMS specifically to fully outfit its automotive labs with essential, up-to-date instructional equipment.

“This program opens doors for a wide range of Mississippians, from recent high school graduates to adult learners and incumbent workers looking to advance their careers,” said Shelika Hooker, director of investments and initiatives at AccelerateMS. “By aligning training with employer needs, Meridian Community College is helping build a stronger workforce and support long-term economic growth in the region.”

“This project reflects the power of strategic investment in education,” said Dr. Lori Smith, dean for workforce education at MCC. “Expanding automotive technology training at Meridian Community College helps align education with workforce demand and creates long-term value for our students, employers, and communities.”

The expansion increases training capacity, and by offering a full associate degree pathway, MCC is strengthening the local talent pipeline and helping meet employer demand. Graduates will be prepared for employment as automotive maintenance and service technicians, with opportunities to advance into specialized repair, diagnostics, and supervisory roles within the automotive and transportation industries.

“I can’t wait to see program graduates securing employment in our community and making a difference for their families,” said Dr. Tom Huebner, MCC president. “We are truly thankful for AccelerateMS’s strategic investment in our region.”

item.title: Man arrested after pop-up party on Monroe Road in Forrest County - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
FORREST COUNTY – A man was arrested after Forrest County deputies responded to a large pop-up party that was blocking traffic and disturbing the area.

The Forrest County Sheriff’s Office said deputies were called May 2 to the Monroe Road area after receiving reports of a loud pop-up party.

When deputies arrived, they found a large crowd gathered at a local venue. During the investigation, deputies determined the venue had not been rented for the event and that people on the property were trespassing.

Deputies spent about an hour clearing the property, according to the sheriff’s office.

Investigators said the party had been advertised as an organized event. The alleged promoter was identified as Cedric Cox.

Cox was arrested and charged with conspiracy to commit malicious mischief and malicious mischief, both felony offenses.

The investigation remains ongoing, and additional arrests are pending, according to the sheriff’s office.

item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:

Lee County Coroner Carolyn Green said Oakland Gober, 53, died of natural causes Thursday.

Green is working to notify Gober’s family of his death. She said Gober had been living at a motel in east Tupelo but previously lived in the area between Tremont and Red Bay, Alabama.

Family members or anyone with information about Gober’s relatives is asked to call Green at 662-687-1852.

item.author: Morgan Howard

JACKSON – Jackson Public Schools is preparing to release a new book highlighting how the district is rethinking STEM education in an era shaped by artificial intelligence and innovation.

item.title: Health Department urges caution during storm recovery - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
JACKSON — The Mississippi State Department of Health is urging residents to use caution while cleaning up after severe storms that moved through the state Wednesday. MSDH said power outages, home repairs and flooding can create dangerous and potentially life-threatening situations.

Residents cleaning up storm-damaged areas should wear protective clothing and sturdy shoes to avoid cuts and scratches from debris. Children should not be allowed to play in floodwater, and any items that come into contact with floodwater should be discarded.

Health officials also recommend tetanus vaccinations for anyone who has not received one in 10 years or more. Anyone with a puncture wound or a wound contaminated by floodwater should contact a health care provider. Tetanus vaccinations are available at county health departments.

MSDH also urged residents to be careful while cleaning up around their homes. Ladders should be secured before use, and chainsaws should be operated according to instructions. Anyone injured during cleanup should call 911 or seek immediate medical help.

Flooding also can cause mold to grow inside homes, which can lead to allergic reactions, asthma episodes, infections and other respiratory problems. MSDH said it does not handle mold removal or abatement and that residents should contact a private contractor for help.

Residents who lost power to refrigerators or freezers for more than four hours should throw out all perishable food. Food stored in coolers should be kept at 40 degrees or below. Food that is still frozen or cold at 40 degrees Fahrenheit or less is safe to prepare, according to MSDH.

Health officials also warned residents about carbon monoxide poisoning. Charcoal or gas grills should not be used inside a house, garage, vehicle, tent or fireplace. Gas-powered generators and pressure washers should not be used indoors, in garages or in other enclosed spaces.

Anyone experiencing symptoms of carbon monoxide poisoning should open doors and windows, turn off gas appliances and go outside. In severe cases, residents should call 911 or the Mississippi Poison Control Center at 1-800-222-1222.

For residents under a boil water alert, MSDH said not to drink tap water or use ice made from recent tap water. Tap water should not be used to make drinks, juices or fountain drinks. Residents should cook with tap water only if the food is boiled for at least one minute and should brush their teeth with boiled or bottled water.

Water should be brought to a rolling boil for one minute to kill most organisms. Active and lifted boil water alerts can be tracked at msdh.ms.gov/boilwater.

Homeowners impacted by flooding who use private wells should have the wells inspected, disinfected and sampled before use, according to MSDH.

item.title: Genuine MS Farmers Market to open May 16 at Rankin County Co-op - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Therese Apel
item.description:
BRANDON — The Genuine MS Farmers Market at the Rankin County Co-op is scheduled to open Saturday, May 16, with state agriculture officials and local vendors celebrating the start of the growing season.

Andy Gipson, commissioner of the Mississippi Department of Agriculture and Commerce, will officially open the market with a ribbon-cutting ceremony at 9 a.m. The market itself will begin operating at 8 a.m.

Gipson said all products sold at the market will be grown, raised or processed in Mississippi.

“It’s the beginning of the growing season, and 100 percent of the products available to shoppers will be Mississippi-grown and raised,” Gipson said in a statement.

The seasonal market will operate every Saturday from 8 a.m. to noon through October 2026.

Officials said the market will feature local vendors selling fresh produce, meat products, honey, specialty foods, plants and other Genuine Mississippi products. A pop-up location of the Genuine MS Retail Store will also be available on-site.

Participating vendors include Two Dog Farm, Pennington Farm Honey, Paul’s Plants, New Ground Nursery, Red River Trading Co., Amason Farms, Cooper Farms and Vineyard LLC, DNA BBQ, Great Southern Blueberries, Nature’s Crest LLC, Beason Family Farm and Buckin’ RR’s Farms LLC.

The market is located at 2861 U.S. 80 in Brandon.

item.title: Forrest County man pleads guilty in unemployment fraud case - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Therese Apel
item.description:
JACKSON — State Auditor Shad White announced Monday that a man has pleaded guilty to one count of fraudulent statements and representations connected to unemployment benefits fraud.

According to the State Auditor’s Office, Benjamin Coleman submitted fraudulent weekly certification sheets in order to obtain unemployment funds from the Mississippi Department of Employment Security.

“My office will continue to drop the hammer on criminals who can be identified and recover as much misspent taxpayer dollars as possible,” White said in a statement.

Coleman was sentenced in Forrest County Circuit Court to three years in the Pre-Trial Diversion Program. He was also ordered to pay $2,824 in restitution and $175 in fines.

The State Auditor’s Office encourages anyone who suspects fraud involving public funds to report it through the Office of the State Auditor website or by calling 1-800-321-1275 during normal business hours.

item.title: Former Calhoun City alderman sentenced in assault, robbery case - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Therese Apel
item.description:
CALHOUN CITY — Former Calhoun City alderman Tony Herrod was sentenced to two years in Chickasaw County court on Monday in connection with a 2024 aggravated assault.

Herrod had been initially charged with aggravated assault and strong-armed robbery after authorities said he and another man chased down and assaulted a victim at the elementary school in Calhoun City.

According to Sheriff Greg Pollan, Calhoun City Police Department requested the Calhoun County Sheriff’s Office investigate the reported attack.

Investigators said the assault happened on a Sunday night in 2024 at the elementary school. The victim told deputies that two or more men chased him down, assaulted him and caused serious bodily injury.

The victim also reported that several items were taken from his pockets during the attack.

Authorities said investigators obtained video footage of the incident and later secured warrants for the suspects.

Herrod’s arrest marked his second arrest within a year at the time. In a separate case, the Tupelo Police Department arrested Herrod after he was accused of taking two wallets from Wall’s Bargain Center on South Gloster Street and assaulting the store’s manager.

item.title: Two girls under 5 found abandoned in Rankin County neighborhood; deputies searching for parents - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Therese Apel
item.description:
RANKIN COUNTY – Authorities are trying to identify the parents of two young children who were found abandoned Sunday evening in the Castlewoods subdivision, according to the Rankin County Sheriff’s Department.

Deputies responded at about 6:47 p.m. to the area near Azalea Court after receiving a report that two children had been left abandoned.

Deputies and residents canvassed the neighborhood for several hours searching for the children’s parents but were unable to locate them.

The children were taken into the custody of the Mississippi Department of Child Protective Services.

The children are described as two black girls under the age of 5.

Authorities said both were wearing matching outfits, though they are not believed to be twins. Their clothing was described as pink shirts with white bows and pink and white skirts.

Anyone who recognizes the clothing description or has information about the children is asked to contact the Rankin County Sheriff’s Department at 601-825-1480.

item.title: Prentiss man killed in Jefferson Davis County crash - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
JEFFERSON DAVIS COUNTY – A Prentiss man was killed Saturday morning in a two-vehicle crash on Mississippi Highway 13, according to the Mississippi Highway Patrol.

Troopers responded to the crash at about 7:56 a.m. May 9 in Jefferson Davis County.

MHP said a 2012 Chevrolet Avalon driven by Christopher O. Jackson, 56, of Prentiss, was traveling south on Mississippi Highway 13 when it collided with a 2005 Chevrolet Suburban driven by Alphonso L. Mingo, 51, of Silver Creek, who was traveling north.

Mingo was taken by ambulance to a local hospital with moderate injuries.

Jackson died from his injuries and was pronounced dead at the scene by the Jefferson Davis County Coroner’s Office.

The crash remains under investigation by the Mississippi Highway Patrol.

item.title: Jackson man arrested after fatal shooting on Sunset Drive - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Therese Apel
item.description:
JACKSON — A 25-year-old man is in custody after a fatal shooting Friday evening at a residence on Sunset Drive, according to the Jackson Police Department.

Police said officers responded around 6:27 p.m. May 9 to the 3500 block of Sunset Drive following a report of an aggravated assault.

When officers arrived, they found an unresponsive man inside the home suffering from multiple gunshot wounds. Authorities identified the victim as 30-year-old Chaleyl Alexander.

Alexander was pronounced dead at the scene, police said. His next of kin has been notified.

Investigators identified the suspect as 25-year-old Mario Marley Jr., who is currently in custody.

The department’s Homicide Unit, Mobile Crime Lab and the Hinds County Coroner’s Office responded to the scene.

Authorities said a motive has not yet been determined and the investigation remains ongoing.

Anyone with information about the case is asked to contact Jackson police at 601-960-1604 or Crime Stoppers at 601-355-TIPS. Officials said tips leading to an arrest may qualify for a reward of up to $2,500.

item.title: UPDATE: Victims in Rankin County double murder/ suicide identified as local firearms family - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Therese Apel
item.description:
BRANDON — Two people were fatally shot Friday afternoon during a dispute over family land in Rankin County, and the suspected gunman was later found dead of an apparent self-inflicted gunshot wound following a hours-long SWAT standoff, authorities said.

Walter E. Birdsong Jr., 62, and Amanda L. Birdsong, 43, were killed in the shooting on the 1400 block of Monterey Road. The suspected shooter, Kurt Tyler Birdsong, 56, was found dead inside a bathroom of the residence after deputies breached the home, according to the Rankin County Sheriff’s Office.

All three were family members involved in an ongoing dispute over land, investigators said. Deputies responded to a 911 call just before 4 p.m. reporting two people had been shot and that the armed suspect had retreated inside a residence on the property. The Rankin County Sheriff’s Office SWAT Team, negotiators and technical response personnel were among those who responded.

Because the family was involved in a firearms-related business, the sheriff’s office requested assistance from the FBI’s Jackson Field Office, the Mississippi Office of Homeland Security, the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives and the Clinton Bomb Squad, citing an elevated potential threat to law enforcement and nearby residents. Neighbors were evacuated as a precaution.

W.E. Birdsong & Associates Inc., located at 1435 Monterey Road in Florence, has operated since 1973 and holds a federal firearms license issued by the ATF. The company is the manufacturer of Black-T, a proprietary weapons coating used by government and military clients, and is widely regarded in the firearms industry as a leading provider of protective gun finishes.

After armored vehicles arrived, SWAT members and negotiators made multiple attempts to contact the suspect, all of which were unsuccessful. Deputies then used armored and technical equipment to breach the home, where they found Birdsong deceased.

Rankin County Deputy Coroner Cliff Dunlap responded to the scene and transported the deceased.

The investigation is ongoing. The sheriff’s office continues to receive assistance from the FBI and ATF Jackson offices.​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​

item.title: State Officials Warn Storm Survivors to Watch for Contractor Fraud During Recovery Efforts - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Therese Apel
item.description:
JACKSON — Mississippi officials are encouraging homeowners affected by recent storms in the southern part of the state to carefully research contractors before agreeing to repair work, citing concerns about fraud and unlicensed construction activity in damaged communities.

The Mississippi State Board of Contractors said periods following severe weather often lead to an increase in questionable repair offers from out-of-town operators and scammers targeting residents eager to rebuild.

“Storm recovery creates urgency, and unfortunately scammers count on that,” Stephanie Lee said in a statement. “We understand families want to rebuild quickly, but rushing into an agreement with an unlicensed contractor can lead to unfinished work, unsafe repairs and significant financial loss.”

The agency said homeowners should verify that contractors are properly licensed before allowing work to begin. Licensed contractors are subject to state oversight and regulatory standards, officials said.

The warning comes as many South Mississippi residents continue cleaning up damage caused by recent storms and severe weather.

According to the Federal Trade Commission, complaints involving home repair scams routinely increase after natural disasters. Officials said warning signs can include contractors going door-to-door, demanding large upfront payments or pressuring residents to sign contracts immediately.

The contractors board recommends that homeowners seek referrals from trusted sources, obtain multiple written estimates and avoid paying the full cost of a project before work is completed. Residents are also urged to insist on written contracts outlining the scope of work, project timeline and payment terms.

Officials said consumers should use traceable forms of payment and report suspicious activity or unlicensed work to the state board.

“Choosing a licensed contractor is one of the most important decisions a homeowner can make after a storm,” Lee said. “Our goal is to help Mississippi families recover safely, responsibly and without becoming victims of fraud during an already difficult time.”

The Mississippi State Board of Contractors regulates the state’s construction industry and investigates complaints involving unlicensed contractors and other violations.

item.title: Purdue-Sackler opioid settlement takes effect, bringing nearly $41M to Mississippi - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
JACKSON – Mississippi is expected to receive nearly $41 million over the next 15 years after a $7.4 billion settlement with Purdue Pharma and the Sackler family became legally effective May 1, Attorney General Lynn Fitch announced.

The settlement caps more than a decade of work by attorneys general across the country over Purdue’s and the Sacklers’ role in the opioid crisis. Mississippi sued Purdue in December 2015, shortly before a multistate investigation was launched.

“The opioid epidemic has claimed far too many lives in Mississippi, leaving behind lasting pain,” Fitch said. “This settlement is another step toward holding accountable those who played a role in this epidemic and toward healing for many Mississippians who lost loved ones. Together, we can address the harm already done and prevent more senseless deaths.”

Purdue filed for bankruptcy in September 2019 amid widespread litigation. Attorneys general have played a lead role in the bankruptcy proceedings.

The settlement resolves litigation against Purdue and the Sackler family for producing and aggressively marketing opioids in the United States. Fifty-five attorneys general representing eligible U.S. states and territories previously signed onto the settlement.

Mississippi is expected to receive $40,958,248.92 from the settlement. Fitch’s office said the latest agreement brings the total amount of opioid settlement funds secured for Mississippi to more than $400 million.

The settlement permanently bars the Sacklers from selling opioids in the United States and provides money for addiction treatment, prevention and recovery programs nationwide.

Under the agreement, Purdue’s manufacturing operations transferred May 1 to Knoa Pharma LLC, which will be overseen by a board of directors with no connection to Purdue. The settlement also prevents Knoa from marketing opioids and requires an independent monitor to ensure the company provides the medicines in a manner intended to limit the risk of diversion.

The settlement also requires Purdue and the Sacklers to make public more than 30 million documents related to their opioid business.

item.title: Mississippi Supreme Court closes door on juvenile lifer's final appeal - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Therese Apel
item.description:
JACKSON — The Mississippi Supreme Court has refused to hear the final appeal of a man sentenced to life in prison for crimes he committed at age 14, ending his decades-long legal fight for the chance at parole.

The state’s high court rejected David Moody’s petition on May 1, 2026, with six justices voting to deny and one voting to grant. The decision leaves intact a Mississippi Court of Appeals ruling from August 2025 that upheld Moody’s life-without-parole sentence.

Moody, now in his mid-40s, has been incarcerated since 2000 for his role in the 1995 deaths of Robbie Bond and William Hatcher in Perry County. He was 14 years old at the time.

The case had worked its way back through the courts after a 2012 U.S. Supreme Court ruling required judges to individually consider a juvenile’s age, background and potential for rehabilitation before sentencing them to life without parole. A three-day hearing was held in Perry County in February 2024, after which the circuit judge decided the sentence should stand. The Court of Appeals agreed, and now the Mississippi Supreme Court has declined to second-guess that decision.

On the night of May 14, 1995, Moody and his older cousin Kenneth Moody were with the young couple at a bridge in Perry County when Kenneth Moody attacked and killed Hatcher, then kidnapped, raped and murdered Bond. David Moody maintained throughout the proceedings that Kenneth threatened to kill him if he did not cooperate, and DNA evidence supported his claim that he did not rape Bond. He came forward to police four days later and led investigators to the bodies.

The former Forrest County sheriff who first took David Moody’s statement testified at the 2024 hearing that the case was “the biggest injustice and travesty of justice” of his 44-year career.

Courts ultimately pointed to David Moody’s prison disciplinary record of more than 60 violations including possession of homemade weapons, contraband cell phones and threatening a corrections officer in concluding he had not shown the capacity for rehabilitation.

A dissenting judge on the Court of Appeals argued the majority placed too much weight on the severity of the crime and not enough on the reality that Moody was a frightened child under the control of a violent older relative with no way to escape. Two justices on the Supreme Court agreed the case deserved a closer look, but were outvoted.

With the state Supreme Court’s refusal to act, Moody has no remaining avenues for appeal within the Mississippi court system.

item.title: Mississippi Insurance Department urges storm victims to document damage, file claims quickly - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Therese Apel
item.description:
JACKSON — The Mississippi Insurance Department is encouraging homeowners affected by the May 6-7 storms to begin documenting damage and contacting their insurance companies as recovery efforts continue across the state.

State officials said residents should first review their insurance deductibles, assess property damage and determine whether filing a claim is necessary.

The department urged policyholders to begin the claims process as soon as possible, noting that some insurance policies contain deadlines for reporting storm-related damage.

Officials also advised residents to gather policy information before filing claims and keep detailed records of conversations with insurance companies, creditors and relief agencies throughout the recovery process.

The agency recommends taking photographs or video of damaged property and creating an inventory of damaged or missing items before insurance adjusters arrive. Homeowners were also advised to save receipts for temporary repairs and emergency expenses.

According to the department, residents should make only temporary repairs needed to prevent additional damage — such as covering broken windows or leaking roofs — until adjusters inspect the property and repair costs are agreed upon.

Officials said homeowners displaced by storm damage should ask insurers whether their policies include coverage for additional living expenses.

The department also cautioned residents to keep damaged personal property available for inspection and to request itemized explanations of claim settlement offers from adjusters.

State officials noted that smaller claims may be resolved quickly, while widespread storm damage could result in longer processing times for larger claims.

Residents needing assistance with insurance questions or claims can contact the Mississippi Insurance Department by phone or through its website.

item.title: MDWFP Announces Temporary Boat Access Restrictions at Two State Parks for July 4 Events - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Therese Apel
item.description:
JACKSON — The Mississippi Department of Wildlife, Fisheries, and Parks announced temporary boat access restrictions at two state parks during Fourth of July holiday events connected to America 250 celebrations.

At Paul B. Johnson State Park, boat access to the lake will be closed from 8 a.m. to 1 p.m. July 3 while water-based activities and holiday events take place.

At Percy Quin State Park, boat access will be limited throughout the day July 3 and July 4 because of scheduled Independence Day celebrations and activities.

Officials said only overnight guests at Percy Quin State Park will be allowed lake access during the restrictions, and those visitors must coordinate with park staff for designated launch and retrieval times.

The temporary restrictions apply only to boat access. Visitors will still be permitted to fish from the banks of the lakes during closure periods, according to MDWFP.

The agency said the adjustments are intended to help ensure public safety during the holiday weekend festivities.

Additional information about America 250 celebrations at Mississippi state parks is available through MDWFP.

item.title: Man known as "BooBay" charged with murder, given $1M bond in Jackson backyard homicide - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
JACKSON – A Jackson man has been charged with murder after he was arrested Wednesday, police said.

The Jackson Police Department said officers responded at about 8:30 p.m. May 7 to the 1800 block of Chadwick Drive, where they arrested Arius Henderson, 38, also known as “BooBay.”

He was arrested in connection with the shooting that happened yesterday when a man was found shot to death in a backyard on Gaites Lane.

UPDATE: Man found shot to death in South Jackson backyard identified

Police said Henderson was taken to JPD headquarters and interviewed before being booked into city holding.

Henderson appeared before a municipal court judge Thursday morning and was given a combined bond of $1 million. Police said the bond included $900,000 for murder and $100,000 for convicted felon in possession of a firearm.

The investigation is ongoing.

Anyone with information is asked to contact the Jackson Police Department at 601-960-1604 or Crime Stoppers at 601-355-TIPS (8477). Crime Stoppers said tipsters may be eligible for a reward of up to $2,500 if information leads to an arrest.

item.title: Man extradited to George County in sexual, physical abuse case - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
GEORGE COUNTY – A man previously arrested in Alabama after an investigation into multiple reports of sexual and physical abuse has been extradited to George County, according to the George County Sheriff’s Office.

Tony K. Fairley, 49, was previously arrested in Baldwin County, Alabama, after an extensive investigation by George County authorities.

The sheriff’s office said Fairley was initially charged with three counts of sexual battery and two counts of child abuse after multiple people came forward reporting incidents that allegedly happened over several years.

Since Fairley’s return to George County, additional charges of molestation and grooming have been filed, according to the sheriff’s office.

Bond was set at $200,000 each for the three sexual battery charges, $50,000 each for the two child abuse charges, $50,000 for the molestation charge and $50,000 for the grooming charge. The total bond amount is $800,000.

Fairley is being held at the George County Regional Correctional Facility pending further court proceedings.

Sheriff Mitchell Mixon said the case reflects the dedication of investigators and the department’s commitment to protecting victims in George County.

The sheriff’s office said the investigation remains focused on protecting the community and holding offenders accountable.

Fairley is presumed innocent unless and until proven guilty in court.

item.title: Lincoln County deputies to offer meals, supplies at Charity Baptist Church in aftermath of storms - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
LINCOLN COUNTY – The Lincoln County Sheriff’s Office said deputies will be back at Charity Baptist Church to provide food and supplies for residents affected by recent storms.

Deputies said they will be at the church beginning at 9 a.m. with coffee and muffins.

At 11 a.m., burgers, hot dogs and tacos will be served. The sheriff’s office said enough food will be available for 600 people.

Deputies also said the grill will be going throughout the day. Residents who have food in their freezers and do not want it to go to waste are encouraged to bring it by so it can be cooked.

Donations will also be available for residents and families, including diapers, wipes, toilet paper, water, toothbrushes, toothpaste, snacks and canned goods.

The sheriff’s office said residents who are unable to get to the church can reach out, and deputies will work to get supplies to them.

item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
GREENVILLE – The Greenville Police Department is investigating an indecent exposure incident reported at Walmart.

Police said the incident happened at about 4:03 p.m. Wednesday, May 6, inside the store.

According to police, an adult female customer reported that she was shopping when she was approached by an unknown man in one of the aisles. The woman told police the man approached her multiple times before engaging in lewd and inappropriate behavior in her presence.

The suspect was described as a Black male, about 5 feet, 6 inches tall, believed to be between 30 and 35 years old. Police said he was wearing a dark-colored jacket.

Detectives reviewed store surveillance footage with loss prevention personnel and obtained still images and video of the suspect near the area where the incident occurred.

Investigators are working to identify the man.

Anyone with information is asked to contact Washington County Crime Stoppers at 662-378-TIPS (8477) or the Greenville Police Department at 662-378-1515.

item.title: Domestic dispute call leads to officer-involved shooting in Corinth - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Morgan Howard
item.description:
CORINTH – The Mississippi Bureau of Investigation is investigating an officer-involved shooting involving the Corinth Police Department.

MBI said the shooting happened May 8 at a home on West Harris Circle in Corinth.

According to MBI, Corinth police officers responded to a domestic dispute at the residence. When officers arrived, they attempted to detain the person involved.

MBI said the person resisted and fired a weapon at officers. One officer then fired their weapon, striking the person.

The person was taken to a nearby hospital in stable condition. No officers received any serious physical injuries, according to MBI.

MBI said agents are assessing the incident and gathering evidence. Once the investigation is complete, findings will be turned over to the Attorney General’s Office.

Officials said the information is preliminary and subject to change. Additional information may be released later.

item.title: At least 5 tornadoes carved paths across south Mississippi Wednesday night - Darkhorse Press
item.author: Therese Apel
item.description:
JACKSON — Two powerful EF3 tornadoes were in a group of at least five twisters that tore across South Mississippi during Wednesday night’s severe weather outbreak, leaving behind long paths of destruction, multiple injuries and hundreds of documented damage sites, according to preliminary findings from the National Weather Service office in Jackson.

The strongest storms included the Garden City tornado, which reached peak winds of 136 mph and traveled 30.7 miles, and the East Franklin-to-Monticello tornado, which packed 137 mph winds along a 35.9-mile path stretching more than a half-mile wide at times.

The Franklin-to-Monticello tornado injured 12 people and grew as wide as 2,050 yards, making it one of the most significant storms of the outbreak. The Garden City tornado injured one person and reached a maximum width of 1,600 yards.

Despite the intensity of the storms, officials said no fatalities were reported in any of the five confirmed tornadoes.

National Weather Service survey teams said they assessed more than 70 miles of tornado tracks and documented 472 separate damage points Thursday. Officials said additional survey work remains underway, including areas in Lamar and Forrest counties that had not yet been fully examined as of Thursday night.

The weather service said more analysis will continue in the coming days using drone footage and high-resolution satellite imagery, and additional adjustments to tornado ratings and path details remain possible.

Officials described the two EF3 tornadoes as the most destructive storms of the evening, particularly the Franklin-to-Monticello tornado because of its length, width and number of injuries.
